To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Military service records for service member;
Name: Daniel McEvoy 
Branch: United States Navy
DOB - 3/7/1945
Dates of Service: Approx yrs 1964 to 1980

Request following documents;
1) copy of Bronze Star medal award citation
2) copy of Navy Commendation Medal award citations
3) History of assignments form NAVPERS 601-5
4) copy of Navy achievement medal citations 
5) Training/Service Schools attended form NAVPERS 601-4
6) list of Awards, date of release from Active Duty, badges
7) Purple heart administrative remarks 
8) Presidential unit citation award letter
Vietnam War
Redact per 5 U.S.C. § 552(b)(6).
I request hard copies of paperwork in the file showing this information.
Please mail hardcopies to:
MUCKROCK NEWS Dept MR#
263 HUNTINGTON AVE
BOSTON, MA 02115

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Eric Bradley

To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Massachusetts Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

Records regarding any automated decision systems, algorithms, data-matching programs, artificial intelligence, machine learning, or predictive analytics used by the EOHHS to assist in determining eligibility, detecting fraud, or flagging cases for review in the Medicaid program.

Procurement contracts and RFPs for third-party software used for fraud detection, identity verification, or eligibility determination.

Documentation of any internally developed software used for fraud detection, identity verification, eligibility determination, or data interfaces that exchange modules in the Medicaid enterprise systems that impact exemptions or exclusions from work requirements pertaining specifically to medical frailty. This request includes, but is not limited to, the following types of records: 
- Change Request Analysis 
- Unit Testing and User Acceptance Testing documentation
- Technical Specifications 
- Details from Change orders, Change Requests, or Tickets from any project management system used to document modifications to this software
- Meeting minutes from status update meetings or project meetings in reference to these technologies, associated change order numbers, or related development

User manuals, policy memos, desk level procedures, work patterns, or training materials describing how EOHHS staff utilize these tools to deny, reduce, or terminate benefits.

Reports of any validation studies or accuracy audits conducted on these systems. 

Information on algorithms or interfaces used specifically for Medicaid eligibility, including, but not limited to: 
- Prioritizing applicants, flagging urgent needs, and assigning waiver slots
- Determining the level of care (LOC) a recipient should receive 
- Generating updated reports that flag improvements to health resulting in a change to the status of an individual’s LOC
- Exempting or excluding applicants from work requirements
- Verifying that an applicant meets work requirements

If third-party vendor materials are deemed exempt trade secrets, this does not exempt the state’s own training materials, user manuals, or policy memos directing state employees on how to utilize the vendor’s tool. 

If any responsive documents contain information that is believed to be exempt from disclosure, we ask that EOHHS produce all segregable non-exempt portions of that record, as required under G.L. c. 66 § 10(a), and identify the specific statutory exemption for each withholding.

I also request that, if appropriate, fees be waived as we believe this request is in the public interest, as suggested but not stipulated by the recommendations of the Massachusetts Supervisor of Public Records. The requested documents will be made available to the general public free of charge as part of the public information service at MuckRock.com, and is not made for commercial usage.

I expect the request to be filled in an accessible format, including for screen readers, which provide text-to-speech for persons unable to read print. Files that are not accessible to screen readers include, for example, .pdf image files as well as physical documents.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Keira Hale
